high_consensus.description: Critical internal contradiction on incident controls. Two opposite kill-switches documented in different sections is a high-likelihood operational failure mode and could worsen outages. Very low effort to fix, very high risk reduction.

Excellent catch on precedence collisions between global safety switch and user-level preference flags. This is actionable and should be codified in acceptance criteria to avoid nondeterministic routing during incidents.

Strong rollout-risk mitigation. Ordering between schema migration and strict validation is a classic breakage vector in multi-repo/submodule environments. Explicit sequencing and compatibility window are essential.
High-value clarification for a safety-critical budget control. Session scope, pre/post-call enforcement, retry behavior, and terminality directly determine whether spending caps actually work.

Valuable operational specification for fallback stability and recovery. Probe cadence, hysteresis, and state persistence are necessary to prevent flapping, though implementation complexity is moderate.
Important billing correctness issue. Ambiguity around reasoning token inclusion can silently under/over-charge and undermine success metrics. Should be decided upfront, not deferred.
Operationally strong recommendation. A concise rollback playbook with verification steps materially improves incident response quality, especially given existing switch-name confusion.

blockers.concern: Cost accounting for `reasoning_tokens` is under-specified and may double-charge or under-charge.
blockers.why_matters: The PRD states output tokens may already include reasoning tokens, but also suggests summing if split. Without provider-specific billing truth rules, ledger and budget enforcement can be wrong, invalidating guardrails and trust.
blockers.location: Technical Considerations §3.1 Token accounting; FR-1/FR-5a/FR-5 cost-ledger requirements
blockers.recommendation: Define exact billing formulas per provider/model, add reconciliation tests against real invoices/sandbox usage, and block rollout until ledger parity is verified.

blockers.concern: Kill-switch semantics are internally contradictory (alias-layer rollback vs endpoint-layer force-to-chat).
blockers.why_matters: The PRD defines multiple incompatible rollback mechanisms: alias-only rollback in Executive Summary/FR-1, but Risks/Decisions also define `LOA_DISABLE_RESPONSES_ENDPOINT` forcing all OpenAI traffic to `/chat/completions`, which would break gpt-5.5 calls with HTTP 400. In an incident, operators may trigger the wrong switch and amplify outage.
blockers.location: Executive Summary; FR-1 Acceptance Criteria; Risks & Mitigation table; Decisions Locked Post-Flatline
blockers.recommendation: Pick one authoritative rollback contract, delete conflicting mechanisms, define precedence/order of env vars vs config flags, and add a single runbook-tested rollback path.

blockers.concern: No canary or percentage rollout strategy for default alias flips.
blockers.why_matters: Changing `reviewer` and `reasoning` globally is high blast radius. A binary flip for all users risks widespread cost/quality/latency regressions before detection, especially for downstream submodule consumers.
blockers.location: FR-2; Success Criteria; Timeline Sprint 2 deliverables
blockers.recommendation: Introduce staged rollout controls (org/project allowlist, % rollout, or phased opt-in), plus real-time error/cost dashboards and automatic rollback triggers.

blockers.concern: Response normalization scope is brittle: only six known `/responses` shapes are supported, while future shapes are explicitly out of scope.
blockers.why_matters: Provider response schemas evolve. If unknown object types appear, parser behavior is undefined (drop content, malformed result, or exceptions), risking silent data loss or outages.
blockers.location: Technical Considerations §3.1; Scope (explicitly out-of-scope future response object types)
blockers.recommendation: Define strict unknown-shape handling now (fail-safe vs pass-through), add schema-version detection, and include contract tests for forward-compat fallback behavior.

blockers.concern: Timeline is unrealistically compressed for multi-provider routing, schema, pricing, fixtures, rollout, and compatibility work.
blockers.why_matters: Sprint 1–3 plus soak are scheduled over ~6 days with significant cross-cutting changes (adapter protocol, config schema, generated maps, 8 caller updates, fallback automation, cost controls). This is a classic schedule risk leading to shortcuts, incomplete testing, and post-merge regressions.
blockers.location: Timeline & Milestones; Scope/Prioritization; FR-1..FR-6 combined scope
blockers.recommendation: Split release into smaller deployable increments (routing first, then alias flips, then pro-flag), add contingency buffer, and define explicit go/no-go gates based on telemetry.

blockers.concern: `endpoint_family` behavior is inconsistent (required/validation-fail vs silent default-to-chat).
blockers.why_matters: FR-1 says missing `endpoint_family` should fail validation, while Technical Considerations says adapter defaults to `chat` if absent. This ambiguity can cause silent misrouting, non-deterministic behavior across tools, and hard-to-debug production failures.
blockers.location: FR-1 Description/Acceptance Criteria; Technical Considerations (Architecture Notes); Risks table last row
blockers.recommendation: Enforce one rule globally: either strict required field everywhere or explicit migration shim with sunset date. Add contract tests for both CLI validation and runtime adapter behavior.
